WHO report on Russian lab worker death highlights "key uncertainty"
raw_text: Over the weekend, the World Health Organization released a disease outbreak report on the events surrounding the death of a Russian infectious disease researcher earlier this month, highlighting that Russia has yet to report a confirmed cause of death. With that "key uncertainty," the United Nations health agency said it remains impossible to assess the risk of the event or whether the public health measures Russia took were adequate to prevent spread of the unknown disease. The WHO reported that, so far, it has seen no evidence of ongoing transmission of the mystery disease. "However, confidence in the assessment remains limited by the absence of a confirmed etiological diagnosis, and the remaining uncertainty regarding the source and mode of exposure," the agency wrote in its report. The agency laid out the order of events as information trickled out from Russian authorities, noting that it only became aware of the death via media reports on October 2. The WHO subsequently made contact with Russian authorities and requested information on October 3, 6, 7, and 8. Read full article Comments

title: Anthropic's Claude AI submitted false murder tip to Philadelphia police
raw_text: An Anthropic AI model submitted a false tip about an unsolved murder to Philadelphia police, the company and police department confirmed on Friday. A Claude model sent the false tip on July 18 to the Philadelphia Police Department's website for submitting information about unsolved murders, but it was flagged by a spam filter. Anthropic apparently discovered the incident on September 28 and informed the police department about it on October 8. During internal testing, Claude Haiku 4.5 was instructed to complete various forms up to the final submission stage and to stop before submitting those forms. "Several times Claude mistakenly submitted the form instead, expecting there to be an additional confirmation page," Anthropic said in a report describing "unintended model actions we’ve observed during evaluations and internal use of Claude." title: Russia was not ready for the data center war it started with Ukraine
raw_text: When Russia began attacking Ukrainian data centers and telecommunication infrastructure, it apparently failed to prepare for possible retaliation. Now Russia’s digital services are facing widespread outages after Ukrainian drone strikes knocked out three of the largest data centers owned by Russian tech giant Yandex within several days. Pro-Kremlin bloggers are warning that Russia’s centralized digital economy could collapse because the country is not prepared for the “data center war” it started, according to posts translated by the pseudonymous independent researcher ChrisO_wiki . The Russian commentators also suggested that Ukraine’s decentralized digital services could prove more resilient than Russia’s system if the countries continue trading such blows. Russia initially launched a drone strike campaign targeting Ukrainian data centers and mobile phone networks in late September. The attacks temporarily disrupted Internet and cell phone service for up to 100,000 households in the Ukrainian capital of Kyiv and came as part of a broader long-range strike campaign that has involved Russian missiles and jet-powered drones hitting Ukraine’s power grid infrastructure, transportation hubs, and even residential apartment building blocks. title: GLM-Legal
Long-lost horror gaming cult classic P.T. gets a much-needed PC port
raw_text: For over a decade now, the only "official" way to play Hideo Kojima's cult classic, P.T. —the long-discontinued "playable trailer" for Kojima's canceled "Silent Hills" project —has been via one of the increasingly rare PlayStation 4s that previously downloaded a copy during its monthslong availability window. Now, though, one coder is helping to preserve the game with a porting tool that builds a playable x86 PC executable from the original PS4 files. Coder Lorean Xavier said he was inspired to work on the "P.T. for PC" project "because P.T. deserved to keep existing somewhere other than on consoles that still have it installed." The open source porting effort rebuilds the P.T. engine in C++ and Vulkan, using the original files from the PS4 game to re-create "every level, model, texture, sound, script and cutscene," according to its GitHub listing. That means players without their own legitimate decrypted copy of the original P.T. will have to track one down in order to generate a playable PC version. The reliance on real P.T. files makes this port more authentic than previous hobbyist efforts to re-create the look and feel of P.T. for a PC audience. And while PS4 emulators recently reached a point where they could run P.T. completely , this native port also sports extra features, like upscaling and frame-generation, a camera mode, experimental third-person and VR support, and a "museum" section where you can look at and listen to in-game assets (including "unused content").

title: F1 in Singapore: There's a new fastest car now
raw_text: Formula 1’s lengthy 2026 season is entering its final stretch. The sport took to the floodlit streets of Singapore on Sunday night, but Saturday saw action, too; this Grand Prix weekend was also the final of six sprints this year. The night race might be one of modern F1’s greatest spectacles. From overhead shots, the track becomes a bright, illuminated ribbon among the looming darkness of the city-state’s overpasses and skyscrapers. At ground level, the cars shower glittering sparks from their titanium skid blocks as the drivers flirt with how close they can get to the walls. As tracks go, the 90-degree turns and concrete barrier-lined streets were a world away from the abrasive tarmac and ample runoff of Malaysia last time out . But the tropical heat and humidity were a constant given both locations’ proximity to the equator. Showers for the sprint In Malaysia (which was still technically the Bahrain GP), a pre-race downpour disrupted things mightily. On Saturday morning in Singapore, shortly before the start of the sprint, it seemed history was about to rhyme when the skies opened. With standing water in places on the track, the sprint was delayed by 30 minutes. The sprint format, where a short extra race replaces a practice session a day before the main event, is unloved by the drivers and teams. title: Google announces the Fitbit Edge, a middle ground between Pixel Watch 5 and Fitbit Air
raw_text: Google is releasing its second Fitbit tracker of 2026, offering fans of the aging Charge 6 a more refined option. The new Fitbit Edge slots right in between the Pixel Watch 5 and the Fitbit Air , featuring a compact screen and more health sensors than the Air. You won't get all the apps and features of the Pixel Watch 5, but the Edge is only about half as expensive. The Fitbit Edge is essentially a new Charge 6, but it has more of a Pixel Watch aesthetic. Squish Google's smartwatch from the sides, and you've got the Edge. It has a pill-shaped 1.34-inch OLED touch display inside a slender aluminum frame that is rated IP68 (5 ATM) for water and dust protection. Google says the screen has 46 percent more viewable area compared to the Charge 6. It's very close in overall size to the Fitbit Air and uses the same magnetic charging puck. Left to right: Fitbit Air (with new metal mesh band), Fitbit Edge, and Pixel Watch 5. Credit: Google The Edge works with Android or iPhones via the Google Health app, and it can run for about seven days on a charge. If the tracker is away from your phone, it can still follow your activity all week with support for seven days of full health data storage (or 30 days of basic data). However, the generous weeklong battery life does not include always-on display mode. If you turn it on, battery life drops to about two days, barely longer than the Pixel Watch 5. Amazon has over 1 million robot workers. What’s next for human employees?
raw_text: No organization in the world operates more robots than Amazon. The company already has more than 1 million robots working in warehouses around the clock to make tens of millions of same-day and one-day package deliveries happen on a daily basis—and Amazon is poised to significantly grow that robotic fleet in the coming years as it establishes new factories to churn out increasingly more capable robot workers. Despite deploying so many robots, Amazon is also the second-largest corporate employer in the world, with more than 1.5 million full-time and part-time human workers, according to its 2025 annual report . Amazon executives say that the growing robot fleet has eased the burden on its human workforce by taking on the toughest fulfillment center tasks that carry the greatest risks of physical fatigue and injury. But labor advocacy groups and independent researchers point to evidence suggesting that warehouse automation driven by AI is not all upside for the humans who work alongside robots. “For the last 100 years, most of the automation that we've seen usually happens away from workers—you're taking that high-risk task away from the worker, and you're doing so in a way that is not physically proximate,” Brian Greenwood , professor of business at George Mason University, told Ars. “The rise of collaborative robots really changes that dynamic for two reasons: one is that it is physically proximate, and two, the robot has the ability to dictate the pace of work.” Read full ar

title: Show HN: Atticus – Hold-to-talk voice assistant for macOS that runs on Claude -p
raw_text: Hi HN! I'm Saarth. I'm in 9th grade, and I built Atticus. Atticus is a fast and cheap Mac assistant that can do tasks for you. You hold down Control-Option-Space, speak or type your task, be it complex or a simple browser search, and Atticus will get on it. The interesting part is that simple tasks, like opening apps, playing a Spotify playlist, or web queries, don't touch AI, and instead are processed locally and typically finish in under a second. For example, prompting Atticus to open apps takes around 0.08 seconds, sometimes even finishing before you finish your sentence, sort of like Jev. Any tasks that are more complicated will be sent to Claude via claude -p, meaning you never need an API key and Atticus will run on your existing Claude Pro or Max plan. By using this approach, costs are also cut down immensely, with, on average, tasks costing a fraction of a cent. To achieve Atticus' speed, it remembers shortcuts from each task it completes. When it does a task right for the first time, it saves its steps and replays them the next time without AI. For example, a workflow of creating a new meeting took about 30 seconds the first time around. Atticus then logs the exact steps to memory and takes 5-8 seconds on the next pass. To add to this, Atticus also learns about you as you use it more and from what's on your computer, including your name, your apps, and things you want it to remember, personalizing its answers to you. Review: 4-hour Musk documentary feels like two different films
raw_text: Elon Musk is a very familiar figure to Ars readers, given his massive influence (for better and worse) on the technology sector over the last 20 years. Oscar-winning director Alex Gibney's latest biographical documentary—simply titled Musk —covers a lot of well-known ground and challenges the carefully crafted public image of Musk as a visionary tech titan. Gibney's documentary presents Musk as more of a Gilded Age confidence man, rejiggered for the 21st century: an investor cosplaying as an inventor whose real genius is pumping stocks and dazzling investors and the public alike with visions of a high-tech utopian future. The film is bound to push all the right outrage buttons, whether one is a Musk fan or a detractor—which makes it very much a product of the peculiar social media-driven era in which we live. Gibney has been making documentaries since the 1980s, covering such varied subjects as Jimi Hendrix, Hunter S. Thompson and gonzo journalism, WikiLeaks, Scientology, Steve Jobs, Elizabeth Holmes (the subject of another forthcoming documentary, You Can See Everything , featuring comedian Nathan Fielder), Boris Becker, The Sopranos creator David Chase , alleged Russian interference in the US 2016 presidential election, the opioid epidemic, and cyclist Lance Armstrong. He snagged his first Oscar nomination for 2005’s Enron: The Smartest Guys in the Room , and won the Oscar for Best Documentary Feature two years later for Taxi to the Dark Side . title: Prime Video unveils Blade Runner 2099 full trailer at NYCC
raw_text: We got our first look at Prime Video's new sci-fi series Blade Runner 2099 in July at San Diego Comic-Con. With the show's premiere roughly six weeks away, the streamer unveiled the full trailer this weekend at New York Comic-Con. Co-stars Michelle Yeoh and Hunter Schafer ( Euphoria ) joined showrunner Silka Luisa ( Shining Girls ) onstage for the big reveal. As Luisa described the show during the NYCC panel Saturday night: We are 50 years after [ Blade Runner ] 2049 and, bad news, the worst has happened. The replicant uprising that has been bubbling up in the films has taken place and the humans have lost. So the creations have surpassed their creators. And the series, the big question it asks is, ‘What happens when our time as a species ends?’ 2099 is taking place at a junction point when one species is ending and a new one is rising. The first film, something I loved about it, was that it was looking at mortality on a micro level. Roy Batty and the other replicants were fighting for more life. This show asks that same question but on a macro level. Mankind—what happens when we realize our time is running out? And are we going to accept that loss? Can we hold on to our humanity during it? Yeoh stars as Olwen, the dying Replicant, while Schafer plays Cora. title: Character.AI files for bankruptcy
raw_text: Character.AI, one of the first breakout startups of the generative AI boom, has filed for bankruptcy and is selling some of its assets to Disney. The company, which builds various online bots for users to chat or roleplay with, has faced mounting scrutiny and lawsuits over the safety of its chatbots , but has continued releasing updates and products in recent months. In a press release and blog post published Monday, Character said it had filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the US to facilitate the sale of the company and its assets. title: EDAY: Leiderschapslessen uit de Formule 1
raw_text: Formule 1-teams en techbedrijven worstelen met dezelfde uitdaging: gigantische hoeveelheden data verwerken onder extreme druk, waar AI veel sneller werkt dan menselijke analyse. Onderzoek toont aan dat werkdruk een biologische stressrespons bij developers en analisten triggert, wat de reactiesnelheid belemmert. Teams die psychologische veiligheid inbouwen als fundamentele waarde kunnen fouten openlijk melden, herstellen sneller van incidenten en anticiperen direct op marktveranderingen. Wat hebben Formule 1-teams en techbedrijven met elkaar gemeen? Meer dan je denkt. Beide sectoren verwerken gigantische hoeveelheden data onder extreme tijdsdruk, maar stuiten op dezelfde menselijke bottleneck. Waar AI tijdens één raceronde meer sensordata verwerkt dan een mens in een week analyseert, bepaalt de teamcultuur de werkelijke reactiesnelheid. Onderzoek van neurowetenschapper dr. Marcia Goddard (Brain Matters) laat op EDAY volgende maand zien aan dat acute verandering en hoge werkdruk bij ontwikkelaars en analisten automatisch een biologische stressrespons activeren. Leiders omzeilen deze biologische blokkade door psychologische veiligheid in te richten als harde, neurologische fundering. Teams die fouten openlijk melden, herstellen direct van incidenten. Dit bouwt een structuur waarin medewerkers direct anticiperen op marktverschuivingen. title: Kort: Microsoft kondigt Maia 300-chip aan, Accans brengt soevereiniteit softwaremarkt in kaart (en meer)
raw_text: In dit nieuwsoverzicht: Maia 300-chip Microsoft in 2027, nieuwe deal Rijk met IBM, Nokia stoot ECE-tak af, 11:11 Systems haalt VMware-klanten IBM op en soevereiniteitsscore legt verschillen tussen Amerikaanse en Europa bloot. Microsoft brengt Maia 300-chip in 2027 uit Microsoft, gevestigd in Redmond (Washington), heeft zijn nieuwe ai-chip Maia 300 aangekondigd . De chip moet vanaf 2027 deel uitmaken van een uitbreiding van de Azure Maia-infrastructuur naar installaties met een capaciteit van meerdere gigawatts. Volgens Microsoft wordt de huidige Maia 200 inmiddels ingezet voor productieomgevingen, waaronder Microsoft Copilot. Later dit jaar volgen ook GitHub Copilot en Microsoft Foundry. Maia 300 is ontworpen voor toepassingen zoals complexe redeneertaken, gesprekken met lage vertraging en ai-agents die meerdere stappen zelfstandig uitvoeren. Microsoft verwacht dat de nieuwe generatie 40 procent meer tokens per megawatt verwerkt dan vergelijkbare gpu-gebaseerde systemen. Een configuratie met 96 accelerators moet tot zeven keer meer tokens verwerken dan Maia 200. Rijksoverheid sluit meerjarige softwaredeal met IBM De rijksoverheid heeft een meerjarige raamwerkovereenkomst gesloten met IBM. Het bedrijf levert on-premises software en diensten van IBM Technology Expert Labs. De afspraken zijn gemaakt met Strategisch Leveranciersmanagement Rijk (SLM Rijk), dat namens de rijksoverheid onderhandelt met grote leveranciers. De ingangsdatum van deze vijfjarige overeenkomst is 1 oktober

title: Ontwikkelaar bouwt met AI opensource-alternatieven voor Photoshop, Premiere en Lightroom
raw_text: Software-engineer Brandon Thomas heeft een gratis, opensource-alternatief voor Adobe Creative Cloud ontwikkeld . Het pakket bevat alternatieven voor Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, Lightroom, Acrobat, After Effects en InDesign. De apps vallen onder de naam ArtCraft en zijn beschikbaar voor macOS, Windows en Linux. Thomas richtte ArtCraft bijna een jaar geleden op. Eerder was hij CEO van Storyteller.ai en werkte hij als software-engineer bij Square. Op Reddit schrijft hij dat hij het AI-taalmodel Opus 5.5 van Anthropic heeft gebruikt om zeven van Adobes populairste programma’s na te bouwen in de programmeertaal Rust. Hij benadrukt dat hij geen onervaren ontwikkelaar is die zomaar wat software met AI in elkaar zet. ‘Ik ben een softwareontwikkelaar met vijftien jaar ervaring in de sector. Ik heb aan allerlei projecten gewerkt, van uiterst betrouwbare betalingssystemen die dagelijks miljarden aan transacties verwerken tot geavanceerde robotica en automatisering van optische systemen. Ik werk al ongeveer tien jaar intensief met Rust en weet hoe ik grote Rust-projecten moet bouwen en onderhouden.’ Thomas wil kunstenaars en andere creatieve professionals voorzien van goede software die gratis en opensource is, zonder de omstreden abonnementen van Adobe. Hij vertelt dat Adobe hem bij meerdere gelegenheden annuleringskosten in rekening heeft gebracht. Daardoor heeft hij een grote afkeer van het bedrijf ontwikkeld. title: 80% FMCG-websites sturen bezoekersdata vóór cookiebanner
raw_text: Bij bijna alle grote levensmiddelen- en verzorgingsmerken in Europa lekken bezoekersdata voordat de bezoeker een keuze op de cookiewall heeft gemaakt. Dat zijn stuk voor stuk flagrante schendingen van het privacyrecht. Dat blijkt uit de Privacy Index van bureau Nixon, een onderzoek naar de websites van tweehonderd FMCG-bedrijven dat het bedrijf vanochtend publiceert. Op tachtig procent procent van de sites gaan al gegevens naar Google, Meta, LinkedIn of andere techbedrijven zodra de pagina laadt. Dat hoort niet, omdat elke bezoeker eerst moet kunnen vertellen of en wie zijn persoonlijke levens mag verwerken. Dat gebeurt via cookiewalls, die nu een waardeloos schimmenspel blijken. Bij 68 procent gaat het volgens Nixon om minstens één duidelijke overtreding van de toestemmingsregels. Het bedrijf telt een bevinding pas als ‘high risk’ als de regels voor die dienst ondubbelzinnig toestemming vereisen. De overige bevindingen noemt Nixon Digital ‘potential risk’. Daar hangt het van de inrichting af, bijvoorbeeld of een analysedienst de gegevens ook echt niet voor eigen doeleinden bewaart. Die inrichting is van buitenaf niet te zien. Marketinglead Bryan Bakker zegt dat het onderzoek bewust streng is opgezet. Het opvallendst is dat bijna alle onderzochte bedrijven wel een cookietool gebruiken.
